clue.text: Part of sign attracts small fly

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sign that draws in a little insect, perhaps a light trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a tiny two-winged insect, a common small fly.

clue.text: Racecourse regenerated Lancashire town

parts.note: something regenerated is made new again
Bury is a town in Lancashire (now Greater Manchester), in north-west England

explanation.surface: A northern town rebuilt around its horse-racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regenerated' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies NEW. Newbury is a racecourse in Berkshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newbury is a well-known English horse-racing venue, in Berkshire.

clue.text: A zealot initially going after finest gemstone

indicators.note: the A and Z pieces are placed after the piece for finest

parts.note: the finest is the top

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of zealot

explanation.surface: A fanatic pursuing the best jewel available.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious mineral, usually yellow, cut as a jewel.

clue.text: Red wine to remain in vehicle with fishing gear

indicators.note: in places the word for remaining inside the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to be is to remain or exist, as in 'let it be'
a net is fishing gear

explanation.surface: An angler stays in the car with his tackle and a bottle of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabernet, short for Cabernet Sauvignon, is a red grape and its wine.

clue.text: Clubs welcome letter from Greece

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
hi is a welcoming greeting

explanation.surface: Golf or social clubs receiving a letter sent from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Roller-coaster, British one, gripped frantically

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: frantically suggests wild movement, so the letters of gripped are jumbled

explanation.surface: A British rider clutching the bar in terror on a fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A big dipper is the British term for a fairground roller-coaster with steep drops.

clue.text: Italian dish gentleman knocked up with essential oil

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for gentleman is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sir is the title or address of a gentleman
otto, or attar, is a fragrant essential oil from rose petals

explanation.surface: A man throws together a quick supper flavoured with aromatic oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked up' reads like 'cooked hastily', but in a down clue it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Delete Times puzzle finally

parts.note: eras are times or periods of history

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of puzzle

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrub out the Times crossword at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it gives ERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or remove, the same as to delete.

clue.text: Exchanging spades somewhere in East London

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
Wapping is a riverside district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: Trading garden tools at a market in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping means trading one thing for another, i.e. exchanging.

clue.text: Closely examine second container

parts.note: a can is a container

explanation.surface: An order to inspect a second box carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan can mean to scrutinise point by point, looking carefully over something.

clue.text: Interrogate unknown after pound endlessly

indicators.note: after places the unknown piece behind the shortened pound
endlessly says the word for pound loses its last letter

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling
Z is an algebraic unknown, as x, y and z are

explanation.surface: Questioning someone about a mystery sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiz someone is to question them closely.

clue.text: Shirt and tie restyled — in this decade?

indicators.note: restyled means remade in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shirt and tie given a modern look, as fashionable now.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirties are the decade of years ending 30 to 39, so the clue asks which ten years the outfit belongs in.

clue.text: Had a fling with a female — it became very heated

parts.note: to fling is to throw, so had a fling means threw

explanation.surface: An affair with a woman that turned passionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a fling' suggests a romance but means tossed.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a fit is an idiom for losing one's temper, getting furiously worked up.

clue.text: Seafood Roy's arranged around empty table

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters go round the outside of the emptied table
arranged means put in a different order, so the letters of Roy's are shuffled
empty removes the inside of table, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Roy lays out shellfish on a bare table.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Large number recalled reportedly sharp fantasy author

indicators.note: recalled, read as called back, means the word for large number is reversed

parts.note: a lot is a large number

indicators.note: reportedly means the next piece is heard, not seen: a word for sharp spoken

parts.note: keen means sharp, as of a blade

explanation.surface: A writer of fantasy remembered by many as having a sharp mind.
explanation.definitionFit: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, classics of the genre.

clue.text: Concert exercises performed at once

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: A concert where the workout routine was done immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer series of classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt can mean immediately, without delay, as in 'payment due prompt'.

clue.text: Wordplay something injected by this writer from the Indian subcontinent

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
a jab is an injection, as in a flu jab
this writer means the setter, me, so I

explanation.surface: A writer from the subcontinent being given a vaccination along with some wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi describes people or things of the Punjab, a region split between India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Left depressed with ale passed around, one cries

indicators.note: passed around says the word for ale goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
low means depressed or downcast

explanation.surface: Someone left feeling down, drinking ale handed round, breaks into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellower is someone who shouts or roars, someone who cries out loud.

clue.text: Age English horse and policeman retired

indicators.note: retired, going back, means the pieces for horse and policeman are read backwards

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, horse
a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: How old the English mounted officer was when he stopped work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is street slang for heroin, which is abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long period of history: an age.

clue.text: Jack at home with cross, that brings bad luck

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
in means at home
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Jack staying in, irritable, sees himself as unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a curse or a person or thing believed to cause misfortune.

clue.text: , Mite eats one's supporting beam

indicators.note: eats means the word for mite takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a mite or jot is a tiny amount
one's is I'S, one (I) plus is (S)

explanation.surface: A tiny bug devours a wooden support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mite' looks like an insect but means a tiny bit; 'one's' is read as 'one is', I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: A joist is a timber or steel beam supporting a floor or ceiling.

clue.text: Travel by bike, first half desert

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: first half takes the opening two letters of the four in bike

explanation.surface: Crossing a desert by bicycle, at least for the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Vet fails disastrously to make celebration

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters of vet and fails are scrambled

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon flunks badly and turns it into a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a day or series of events of public celebration.

clue.text: Health resort son has joined annually

parts.note: PA is per annum, meaning annually

explanation.surface: A son becomes a yearly member of a health resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a place with mineral springs visited for health treatments.

clue.text: Beverage: a tin each is drunk

indicators.note: being drunk means unsteady and mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink: everyone downs a can of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is drunk' looks like the drink being consumed but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is tea grown in China, such as Lapsang souchong, a drink.

clue.text: Neat edge on front of topiary

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the edge piece after the other
front of picks the opening letter of topiary

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A tidy border cut on the front of a hedge sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim as an adjective means tidy and well kept, the same as neat.
